---
title: "NFL Draft Predictor"
author: "Sean Gretzinger"
date: "2026-10-22"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(nflreadr)

DraftData <- load_combine(seasons = 2000:2025)
DraftData <- as.data.frame(DraftData)

#Now we have to switch the nas from Draft_round to 0 to say the didnt get drafted, and put the rest of the rounds 1-7 as a 1 for binary
DraftData$Drafted <- ifelse(is.na(DraftData$draft_round), 0, 1)

#Our height is currently in a weird format, we are going to change it to inches for a better prediction
DraftData$InchHeight <- as.numeric(sub("->*", "", DraftData$ht)) * 12 + as.numeric(sub(",*-", "", DraftData$ht))

#The positions can be factored down 
DraftData$pos <- as.factor(DraftData$pos)
#Now we have a better height we can drop the original
DraftData$ht <- NULL

#After running the model originally, we saw that Kickers, Punters, and other specialists are almost automatically drafted if they go to the combine
DraftData <- DraftData[!(DraftData$pos %in% c("K", "P", "LS")), ]
#Additionally, we are going to factorize the draft year, so we no longer need the season 
DraftData$season <- NULL
#We can make the college teams that they get drafted from a factor as well, and additionally, we can do the same with the team they get drafted to 
DraftData$draft_team <- as.factor(DraftData$draft_team)
DraftData$school <- as.factor(DraftData$school)
#With Draft Year as a factor, we can eliminate the need for season
DraftData$draft_year <- as.factor(DraftData$draft_year)

#Nowe we need to run the regression model 
logit.model <- glm(Drafted ~ InchHeight + wt + forty + vertical + pos, data = DraftData, family = "binomial")

```

```{r}
summary(logit.model)
```
